name: tic tak toe
detail: Added the MIT-licensed aminbazai browser build after testing it against PrinterNB. Native player sessions passed in iPad-sized landscape and portrait emulation; commit is ready for trusted verification.

quality.evidence: Played local PvP to X wins and vs AI to an AI win, then retried to 9 open cells in iPad touch emulation. Landscape screenshot: .game-addition-qa/ipad-landscape.png; portrait: .game-addition-qa/ipad-portrait.png; warm reopen: .game-addition-qa/ipad-warm-landscape.png. No page errors or failed requests; no ads, accounts, or remote assets in selected build.

selection.reason: Both versions completed local PvP and AI sessions with correct win feedback and retry. PrinterNB adds board sizes, difficulty settings and a Worker-backed online mode, but its interface is less finished and the online service is not part of its self-contained local build. The aminbazai version has polished responsive controls, score tracking, two complete local modes and a tactical AI; it passed landscape/portrait touch-emulation sessions and warm reopen without external assets or runtime errors.

candidates.evidence: Played PvP through an X win and AI mode through an AI win, then started a fresh round. Its win/block/center/corner AI responded, score changed, and the responsive board and controls fit landscape and portrait touch emulation. Screenshots: .game-addition-qa/ipad-landscape.png and .game-addition-qa/ipad-portrait.png; no runtime errors or failed requests.

Played Human vs Human to an X win, reset and placed another move, then played Human vs AI to an AI win and retried with all 9 cells open. The source also includes 3–6 board PvP, AI difficulty options and a Worker-backed online mode. Screenshot: /tmp/PrinterNB.png; no page errors in the local sessions.
